quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross in front of you. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. Always watch carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Move all four wheels off the road if you can.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move all four wheels off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down, move it completely off the road if possible. Keep all four wheels away from traffic.

questions.question: When a blind person with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always let them cross first.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to let them cross at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use guide dogs or white canes. Always let them cross, no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Let pedestrians in the intersection go first only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians in the intersection pass.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road connects from the right.
The road ahead curves sharply right then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves sharply right then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther away than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away than normal.
questions.explanation: Your car needs more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always keep a longer distance behind the car in front of you when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you better, even if they don't help you see much more.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatal crash.
You should increase your following distance as you drive faster.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 mph, survival in a crash is very unlikely. Faster speeds require longer distances to stop, so you must increase your following distance when you drive faster.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds. Only staring straight ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive carefully through and do not look at the work or accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through and do not look at the work or accident.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual sights. This slowing causes traffic congestion. Drive carefully and keep your attention on the road.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They vibrate and make noise to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They vibrate and make noise to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create vibration and noise to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle cannot completely cross to the other side.
The crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle cannot completely cross to the other side.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your entire vehicle clears the tracks before you stop. Never stop with any part of your vehicle on the tracks.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If your lane has a green arrow signal, you may go in the direction of the arrow when it is safe. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking facing downhill on any road, or facing uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so your vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: As your speed increases, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant in any amount. It slows nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces self-control and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to yield to you.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may pull into traffic without seeing you.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes the driver's hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It draws the attention of other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes the driver's hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even experienced drivers increase their crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before the turn is complete.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This helps other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that the light will soon turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep moving and safely leave the intersection.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving and safely leave the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, move through it as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Do not move until it is safe to completely and clearly pass through the intersection.

questions.question: When leaving a parking space parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Turn on the correct turn signal.
Look over your shoulder.
Do both of these things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of these things.
questions.explanation: If parked on the right side, turn on your left signal and look over your left shoulder before moving into traffic. If parked on the left side of a one-way street, turn on your right signal and look over your right shoulder.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:

options.text: Slows down traffic.
Prevents rear-end accidents.
Improves traffic flow by preventing accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down just to look at accidents or unusual events. This habit, called "rubbernecking," causes traffic to move more slowly.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They go away if you have one mirror on each side of your vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by using your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be careful and watch for danger. Slow down when you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are nearing a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
You will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
You must stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are nearing a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is coming. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must let traffic that might cause a conflict pass first.
Must let vehicles on your right pass.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let traffic that might cause a conflict pass first.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in your path go first. Be ready to stop, but you can keep going if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while driving, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if you need to. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, when should you reduce your speed?

options.text: Only if you want to.
Before you enter the curve.
When you are halfway through the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. This way you will not need to brake hard while in the curve. Braking in a curve can cause a skid and make your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection ahead and have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that makes you take quick action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for the "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: You have stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive forward until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When must you give the right-of-way to a pedestrian?

options.text: When they are in a marked crosswalk.
When they are in any crosswalk or intersection.
When they are crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, drivers should yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle sign means you must yield. When you see a yield sign, slow down to a safe speed and stop if needed. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon. Traffic must move to the left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Traffic must move to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that there will be fewer lanes ahead and traffic needs to merge left.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. Any alcohol can hurt your judgment and coordination. Driving under the influence, even with a low alcohol level, can lead to criminal charges.
